Why is default-allow-ssh risky, and what should I replace it with?

default-allow-ssh allows SSH (tcp:22) from 0.0.0.0/0 to every instance on the default network with logging disabled (FW-001 CRITICAL, FW-006, FW-007, FW-009). Internet-exposed SSH is constantly brute-forced. Replace the source with the IAP TCP forwarding range 35.235.240.0/20, scope it to tagged instances or a service account, enable logging and connect with gcloud compute ssh --tunnel-through-iap (KB-IAP-ADMIN).
